Basic ATC

Expect vectors

An advisory indicating that the pilot should anticipate receiving radar vector instructions from ATC at a specified time, altitude, or fix, typically used to sequence traffic or guide aircraft to a specific point.

Quick answer: An advisory indicating that the pilot should anticipate receiving radar vector instructions from ATC at a specified time, altitude, or fix, typically used to sequence traffic or guide aircraft to a specific point.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Expect vectors?

In this glossary, Expect vectors refers to: An advisory indicating that the pilot should anticipate receiving radar vector instructions from ATC at a specified time, altitude, or fix, typically used to sequence traffic or guide aircraft to a specific point.

How is Expect vectors used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "N123AB, expect vectors for the ILS approach runway 27 at waypoint ALPHA."

Why does Expect vectors matter in aviation?

Expect vectors matters because it supports clear communication in Basic ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Expect vectors?

Expect vectors is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Expect vectors belong to?

In this glossary, Expect vectors is grouped under Basic ATC. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.

Definition
